chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hafs al-Baya' al-Sabiri, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the most beloved ways to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are two sips: a sip of anger that is repelled by forbearance, and a sip of calamity that is repelled by patience.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two most beloved ways to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), highlighting the Prophet’s teaching that suppressing anger and enduring calamity with patience are among the most beloved acts to God. This hadith serves as a cornerstone of Shia ethical theology, framing emotional regulation not merely as self-control but as a spiritual 'sipping' of divine proximity, reinforcing the concept of *hilm* (forbearance) as an active, virtuous response to provocation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hafs Baya’a Al Sabiry, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who loves the Way to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic should swallow two portions – the potion of anger repelling it by the forbearance, and a portion of difficulties repelling it with patience’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Hafs Bayya’ al-Sabiri from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

Of the most beloved path to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, there are two drops: The drop of anger that one brushes aside and repels with tolerance and the drop of suffering that one wipes off with patience.’”
